verdict: Textron's revenue rose 4% to $3.8B as Citation jet deliveries jumped, and earnings per share rose to $1.56 even though Bell's military revenue slipped.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted, from continuing operations, vs $1.31 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $1.76

kpis.label: Textron Aviation revenue
kpis.note: up 14% YoY — 51 Citation jets delivered, vs 42 a year ago

kpis.label: Manufacturing cash flow
kpis.note: before pension contributions (non-GAAP), vs $281M a year ago

segments.name: Textron Aviation
segments.note: Cessna and Beechcraft planes — Citation jets and turboprops, plus parts and servicing. Aircraft revenue rose $152M on higher jet volume and mix, and aftermarket revenue rose $49M.

segments.name: Bell
segments.note: Helicopters for the military and commercial customers. Revenue fell on lower volume on the MV-75 Cheyenne military program and lower commercial deliveries.

segments.name: Textron Systems
segments.note: Defense products and services — armored vehicles, drones and military training (including ATAC). Growth came from armored land vehicles and training services.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.note: E-Z-GO golf cars and other specialized vehicles, plus Kautex fuel systems for cars. Specialized Vehicles grew 9%; Kautex fell 5%. Textron plans to separate this business.

segments.name: Finance
segments.note: Financing customers' purchases of Textron products — a small captive finance arm. A year ago it booked $11M of gains selling off non-captive assets.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new aircraft and defense products — down 7% YoY.

opex.name: Selling & administrative
opex.note: Selling products and running the company day to day — up 5% YoY.

otherDetail: Pension and postretirement income of $70M (the non-service part — returns on pension assets, not an operating cost), less $32M of net interest expense — a net $38M gain below operating income.

takeaways.title: Jets carried the quarter
takeaways.text: Textron Aviation revenue rose 14% to $1,680M, with 51 Citation jets delivered versus 42 a year ago, and its backlog held at $8.0B. Segment profit rose only 4% to $179M, held back by manufacturing inefficiencies.

takeaways.title: Bell is the soft spot
takeaways.text: Bell revenue fell 9% to $933M and segment profit fell 17% to $76M on lower MV-75 program volume. After quarter-end the Army won Congressional approval for extra MV-75 funding, which helped Textron raise its full-year outlook.

takeaways.title: Adjusted profit beat the GAAP print
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS was $1.76 versus $1.56 GAAP — the gap is a $36M LIFO inventory charge (an accounting method that raises cost of sales when prices rise) and $7M of intangible amortization, both before tax. Textron raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $6.55–$6.65.
